title: Bypassing a SaaS that lives on a shared cloud storage or CDN domain

exact-subdomain-only.statement: When one S3 bucket, Blob container or CloudFront distribution must be exempted, exempt its exact hostname (for example `mybucket.s3.amazonaws.com`) and never the shared parent domain.
exact-subdomain-only.conditions: Combination of the guide's warning about shared storage parents and its advice to prefer the most specific domains; the guide does not give a bucket example.

parent-exemption-is-exfil-path.statement: A parent-domain exemption on shared storage becomes an uninspected path for any subscriber's storage account, including one an attacker controls, so it is a data-exfiltration channel as well as a malware one.
parent-exemption-is-exfil-path.conditions: The guide says no inspection occurs for any account; naming the effect as exfiltration is the conclusion drawn here.

googleusercontent-wildcard.title: Whether a wildcard on googleusercontent.com carries the same risk
googleusercontent-wildcard.detail: Unverified legacy statement: `*.googleusercontent.com` is named with `*.s3.amazonaws.com`, `*.blob.core.windows.net` and `*.cloudfront.net` as a wildcard bypass to avoid. The guide names only the AWS, Azure and CloudFront domains; the Google case is tracked as zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions:googleusercontent-exemption.
